newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher due to rise in JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher due to rise in JGBs.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract closed higher on Monday, in sympathy with a rise in Japanese government bonds, as many traders took a wait-and-see stance.

"The only thing that happened was that some buying appeared toward the close, due to a rise in JGBs," a city bank trader said. Few market players were active, as many traders adopted a wait-and-see stance at the start of the new week, he said.
Turnover of the September was a sparse 13,988 contracts.
The city bank trader said the September was heavy on the upside at 99.20.
The market will be watching October machinery orders data, due on Tuesday, traders said.

"I think the common market view is that it (the September) will react to figures that show the weakness of the economy, but that there will not be much effect from figures that are positive for the economy," a trader for another city bank said.
The first trader said the market will not be surprised if the machinery orders data turns out to be strong.
"I think the market has already factored the possibility of machinery orders data turning out to be strong," the first trader said.
The Bank of Japan drained 300 billion yen from the money market on Monday, maintaining a neutral stance.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate is likely to be 0.50 percent on Monday, which would be the same as Friday's weighted average, traders said.
The key overnight call rate was traded heavily at 0.50 percent in the morning before easing in the afternoon, a trust bank trader said.
About 200 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued on Monday at 0.51 percent, traders said.
About 100 billion yen worth of two-month CDs was issued also at 0.51 percent.
About 60 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.50 percent.
